seededInputCapability.integrationPolicy: Treat this as an external pinned producer capability. Do not cherry-pick it into this task and do not implement a competing send-keys or shell-input path. Coordination code may consume or characterize this interface behind a narrow adapter and fake it in tests.

objective: Implement the bounded Coordination Core vertical slice that replaces pane scraping for one structured task to builder handoff to exact-SHA review to acceptance cycle, with durable status/events and provider-native pointer delivery integration.

required: Versioned strict record schemas and validation for workstream/role contract, plan reference, task assignment/claim, exclusive write lease, builder handoff, exact-SHA review request/result, one correction task reference, final acceptance, release handoff, append-only event, and compact current status.
Controller-owned durable SQLite state and private immutable content-hashed artifacts with transactional publication/transition semantics, restart recovery, and idempotent mutation outcomes.
Role/capability enforcement proving exactly one builder lease; orchestrator cannot hold it or submit review; reviewer is read-only unless an explicit scoped small-fix transfer is recorded.

Controller operations and cockpit-core ctl plus mcp-stdio tools sufficient for task publish/claim, artifact read/publish, handoff submit, review request/submit, acceptance submit, release-handoff submit, status, bounded event list, and one-shot wait.
Exact full Git SHA and artifact-hash binding from builder handoff through review and acceptance; stale base/head/hash/role/revision transitions fail without mutation.

A narrow provider-native seeded first-turn adapter that passes a protected prompt-file pointer envelope using the pinned four-flag interface and records acknowledgement as structured state. Terminal text, titles, captures, copy mode, and scrolling are never semantic inputs.

A deterministic isolated rehearsal exercising one complete builder-to-reviewer-to-acceptance cycle and a characterization/checkpoint wrapper for later Choir-flow cutover. Do not touch an active Choir-flow turn.
Concise operator/protocol documentation and focused false-pass-resistant tests.
explicitlyOutOfScope: Generalized workflow engines or arbitrary workflow execution
CI orchestration or replacement of release-conductor gates
Wholesale Cockpit rewrite or multi-instance worker fabric
Raw send-keys delivery, pane scraping, pane titles, or terminal output as semantic authority
Live workstream migration, install, deployment, merge, or production cutover
More than one builder, one bounded reviewer, or one correction loop

implementationGuidance: Extend the existing cockpit-core Go binary and authenticated controller boundary on the pinned base. Do not create a second daemon, second policy stack, or MCP-owned state.
Keep coordination domain code separate from pane/tmux mechanics and split files/packages by responsibility instead of growing existing giant files.

Use strict JSON decoding with unknown-field rejection for mutations, explicit byte/list limits, SHA-256 over stored canonical bytes, no-replace artifact publication, SQLite foreign keys, synchronous durability, and one transaction for transition + event + projection + idempotency result.
Prefer a minimal coherent vertical API over implementing every future candidate operation. Methods may be coordination-prefixed to avoid collision with the pane-control protocol.
Use server-authenticated role assignments; never trust a role claimed in mutation payloads.
Use isolated temporary roots, repositories, and fake seeded launcher/provider in tests. Never connect tests to the live cockpit tmux socket or mutate the protected checkout.
If a design choice would expand scope or conflict with the pinned seeded-input interface, stop and report the exact structured decision needed rather than improvising.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A complete task, claim/lease, handoff, review, acceptance, and release-handoff rehearsal is driven only by structured controller records and events.
Plausible partial/truncated terminal text cannot transition state or produce completion.
Provider-native prompt-file pointer delivery is hash/byte/request bound and independent of copy mode or scrolling; no send-keys route exists.
Builder handoff, review request/result, acceptance, and release handoff bind to one exact full head SHA and declared artifact hashes.
Wrong role, stale revision/base/head, wrong artifact hash, reused idempotency key with changed intent, and duplicate lease all fail without repository or workstream mutation.
Orchestrator cannot hold the builder lease or submit review; reviewer cannot write absent a recorded scoped lease transfer.
Compact status, cursor-based bounded events, and one-shot wait are sufficient for release-conductor monitoring and leak no watcher.
Crash/restart preserves artifacts, claims, lease, event cursor, projection, and idempotent outcomes without duplicate publication/effect.
Existing focused Cockpit tests remain green; the task adds no generalized workflow, CI, or Lean Runner surface.
A committed clean-worktree handoff supplies exact base/head, bounded diff summary, focused checks, known limitations, and output hashes.

focusedVerification: Run relevant new Go unit/integration tests while iterating.
Run targeted protocol/golden corpus checks for new schemas and CLI/MCP parity.
Run the deterministic end-to-end rehearsal and crash/idempotency fault tests.
Run existing directly affected package and Bash characterization tests.

repository: Committed implementation and focused tests on feat/structured-workstream-coordination

handoff.delivery: Return the structured handoff payload in the final response for orchestrator publication; do not write coordination artifacts directly.

stopConditions: Stop after one committed, clean, structured builder handoff.
Stop and report a precise blocker if the pinned base, assigned worktree, sole-writer lease, source pins, or seeded-input dependency cannot be honored.
Do not run a consolidated pre-deployment gate; release-conductor owns it.
Do not merge, install, deploy, or start a live cutover.
